TIL: The original Super Mario game was designed on graph paper

Another interesting fact about that game: Goombas are just mushrooms with legs and different colors. The clouds and bushes were also the same, just different colors.

It's crazy to look at how advanced the later NES games like SMB3 or Kirby's Adventure are considering it was the same console.

The first stage is set up like a tutorial... especially the first couple of steps.

The Goomba falls off the pipe so you have to jump not to die. More often then not, you'll jump right at the point where Mario hits the question brick making the mushroom come out. The brick will probably drop you down onto the Goomba killing him. The mushroom then bounces off the pipe into Mario, causing you to grow.

You just learned a lot about the game.

I eventually quit buy buy caffeine free Coke and switching out regular Cokes. It took a while but eventually I was down to just a cup of coffee in the morning and caffeine free Coke all day. Then I quit drink Coke because it's too much sugar. No if I miss my morning cup of coffee it's no big deal.

I actually have an aversion to caffeine. So if I have more than a tiny little bit, I get an optical migraine. So I have gone my whole life without chocolate, coffee and colas. I try one every year or so to see if my reaction has gone away, but it's still there.

I used to down ~12 cans of diet coke in a day more often than I like to admit. I ended up giving up soda completely, I had horrible headaches before I remembered I still had to drink something and it should be water. This was before I started drinking coffee

I now drink anywhere from 2-6 cups of coffee a day, 4 cups is the 'safe/healthy' limit. There are health benefits of coffee (not caffeine specifically) if you stay at or under that limit. Whenever I go a few days without coffee I really don't feel any sort of withdrawal, and the only negative thing I've ever experienced from coffee is stained teeth.
